bg-23-02.hint: I bought a gift intending to give it to a friend.

bg-23-02.why: -(으)려고 하다 expresses the speaker's future plan or intention.

steps.en: I bought a gift intending to give it to a friend.

bg-23-02.q: How is the writer preparing for the trip?

items: Express general intentions and purposes with -(으)려고 across any action verb
Formulate future plans and ambitions using -(으)려고 해요

bg-23-03.q: Write one sentence saying you decided to meet your friend at 2 o'clock using 2시에 and 만나기로 했어요.
bg-23-03.why: Use -기로 했어요 to state an agreed plan or personal decision.

steps.en: I decided to exercise every day.

ko: 건강을 위해 매일 아침 조깅을 하기로 했어요.
그리고 밤에는 스마트폰을 멀리 두고 일찍 자기로 했어요.
en: The new year arrived, so I set new goals.
For my health, I decided to jog every morning.
And at night, I decided to put my smartphone far away and sleep early.

bg-23-03.q: What morning resolution did the writer make?
bg-23-03.why: The text states '매일 아침 조깅을 하기로 했어요' (I decided to jog every morning).

bg-23-03.q: What bedtime habit did the writer decide to adopt?
options: Putting the smartphone away and sleeping early
bg-23-03.why: The text states '밤에는 스마트폰을 멀리 두고 일찍 자기로 했어요' (I decided to put my smartphone far away and sleep early).

items: State agreed plans, resolutions, and promises with -기로 하다
Conjugate decisions naturally in the past tense (-기로 했어요)

bg-23-04.hint: I am going to the cafe to meet a friend.
bg-23-04.why: Pairing movement verb 가다 with purpose uses -(으)러: 만나러 가요.

bg-23-04.q: Write one sentence stating that you decided to go to Korea using 한국에 and 가기로 했어요.
bg-23-04.why: To express an agreed decision or firm resolution, attach -기로 했어요.

bg-23-04.hint: 빌리다 is not a movement verb (like 가다/오다), so use -(으)려고: 읽으려고.
bg-23-04.why: -(으)러 can only be followed by directional movement verbs like 가다 or 오다. For general verbs, use -(으)려고.

bg-23-04.h: Movement Purpose -(으)러 vs General Intention -(으)려고 vs Decision -기로 하다

a.d: Expresses the purpose of going or coming somewhere; ONLY paired with movement verbs (가다, 오다, 다니다).
ex: 밥을 **먹으러** 식당에 가요. / I am going to the restaurant to eat.
친구를 **만나러** 공항에 왔어요. / I came to the airport to meet a friend.

b.d: Expresses general intention or goal to do something; can be paired with any main action verb.
ex: 친구에게 **주려고** 선물을 샀어요. / I bought a gift to give to a friend.
한국에 **가려고** 비행기 표를 예매했어요. / I booked a flight ticket intending to go to Korea.

bg-23-04.tip: Check the main verb: if it is a movement verb like 가다/오다, use -(으)러; if it is an ordinary action verb like 사다/공부하다, use -(으)려고; for agreed commitments or firm resolutions, use -기로 하다.

steps.en: I go to the cafe to meet a friend.
I go to the cafe on the weekend to meet a friend.

ko: 민우 씨는 주말에 친구와 축구를 하기로 했어요.
경기 후에 마시려고 시원한 물도 챙겼어요.
en: Minwoo decided to play soccer with his friend on the weekend.
He went to the local sports ground to play soccer.
He also packed cold water intending to drink it after the match.

bg-23-04.q: What did Minwoo decide to do with his friend?
bg-23-04.why: The text states '주말에 친구와 축구를 하기로 했어요' (He decided to play soccer with his friend on the weekend).

bg-23-04.q: Why did Minwoo pack cold water?
options: Intending to drink it after the match
bg-23-04.why: The text states '경기 후에 마시려고 시원한 물도 챙겼어요' (He also packed cold water intending to drink it after the match).

items: Avoid mistakenly attaching -(으)러 to non-movement main verbs
